extracted.intended_audience: Citizens, policymakers, and ratifiers considering adoption of the U.S. Constitution (readers of The Federalist Papers / New York public)
extracted.subtask_description: Explanation and defense of the powers delegated to the federal government and the restrictions placed on the States by the proposed U.S. Constitution, with historical rationale and examples illustrating necessity and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to regulate commerce among the several States and the Indian tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: A federal authority 'to regulate commerce among the several States and the Indian tribes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained as necessary to prevent inter-state tolls, imposts, and unfair duties that would burden importers/exporters and create animosities; examples cited from Switzerland, Germany, and the United Netherlands to illustrate dangers of weak central regulation. Without it, regulation of foreign commerce would be incomplete and ineffective; it relieves States that import/export through other States from improper contributions levied by transit States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to coin money and regulate its value (including foreign coin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Power 'to coin money, regulate the value thereof, and of foreign coin.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformity in the value of current coin is necessary; leaving value of foreign coin to individual States could destroy uniformity. This supplies a material omission in the Articles of Confederation. Prevents multiplicity of currencies and related inconveniences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to provide for punishment of counterfeiting current coin and United States securities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to provide for the punishment of counterfeiting the current coin and securities of the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attached to the power to secure the value of coin and securities; securing value requires punishment of counterfeiters. Presented as a natural adjunct to coin-regulating authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to fix the standard of weights and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to fix the standard of weights and measures.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transferred from the Articles of Confederation; analogous to coin regulation—necessary for commercial uniformity and to avoid confusion among States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to establish a uniform rule of naturalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to establish a uniform rule of naturalization throughout the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified by the confusion and injustices arising from differing State rules that could allow aliens to acquire rights in one State incompatible with another; uniformity prevents circumvention of disabilities by moving between States and avoids serious embarrassments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to establish uniform laws of bankruptcy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to establish uniform laws of bankruptcy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connected to regulation of commerce; prevents frauds where parties or property move across State lines and addresses procedural complications that arise from differing State bankrupt laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to prescribe how public acts, records, and judicial proceedings shall be proved and enforced across States
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to prescribe the manner in which the public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of each State shall be proved, and the effect they shall have in other States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as an improvement over the Articles of Confederation where the meaning was indeterminate; can be a convenient instrument of justice, especially on borders where effects may be secretly translated into another jurisdiction during process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to establish post offices and post roads
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to establish post offices and post roads.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered a harmless and potentially highly convenient power that facilitates intercourse between States and public convenience when judiciously managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to promote the progress of science and useful arts (copyrights and patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to promote the progress of science and useful arts, by securing, for a limited time, to authors and inventors, the exclusive right to their respective writings and discoveries.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility of securing copyrights and patents is defended as aligning public good with private claims; States cannot separately make effective provisions, so federal provision is appropriate and many States already anticipated it by laws at Congress's instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive legislation over federal district and places purchased for federal use
rubrics_metrics.description: Power 'to exercise exclusive legislation, in all cases whatsoever, over such district (not exceeding ten miles square) as may...become the seat of the government of the United States; and to exercise like authority over all places purchased...for the erection of forts, magazines, arsenals, dockyards, and other needful buildings.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary to ensure complete authority at the seat of government and protect public property and installations from State interference; circumscribed extent and requirement of State concurrence in cession obviate many objections; municipal legislature for local purposes may be allowed, and inhabitants' rights are to be provided for by the ceding State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to declare the punishment of treason with limits on consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to declare the punishment of treason, but no attainder of treason shall work corruption of blood, or forfeiture, except during the life of the person attained.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional definition and fixed proof required are a barrier against politically abused definitions of treason; restricting collateral consequences (no corruption of blood or forfeiture beyond life) guards against dangerous extensions of punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to admit new States into the Union with consent constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to admit new States into the Union; but no new State shall be formed or erected within the jurisdiction of any other State...without the consent of the legislatures of the States concerned, as well as of the Congress.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrects omission in the Articles of Confederation; requires concurrence of federal authority and affected States to prevent partitioning or unwanted unions of States and to quiet jealousy of both large and small States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to dispose of and make rules respecting federal territory and property (with proviso)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to dispose of and make all needful rules and regulations respecting the territory or other property belonging to the United States, with a proviso, that nothing in the Constitution shall be so construed as to prejudice any claims of the United States, or of any particular State.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A power of great importance required by similar considerations as for other federal powers; proviso included to guard against jealousies and protect preexisting claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to guarantee each State a republican form of government and to protect against invasion and domestic violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to guarantee to every State in the Union a republican form of government; to protect each of them against invasion; and on application of the legislature, or of the executive (when the legislature cannot be convened), against domestic violence.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guaranty defends the union from aristocratic/monarchical innovations; federal protection against invasion and, upon appropriate application, domestic violence, is necessary to preserve republican institutions and to support weaker members against more powerful neighbors or internal violent combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to consider pre-Constitution debts and engagements valid
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision 'to consider all debts contracted, and engagements entered into, before the adoption of this Constitution, as being no less valid against the United States, under this Constitution, than under the Confederation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaratory in nature to assure foreign creditors and maintain moral obligations; asserts continuity of obligations and rebuts the idea that change in political form dissolves moral responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to provide for amendments ratified by three fourths of the States (with two exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority 'to provide for amendments to be ratified by three fourths of the States under two exceptions only.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mode for amendments balances preventing extreme facility (too mutable) and extreme difficulty; enables both general and State governments to originate amendments; exceptions protect equality of suffrage in the Senate and other safeguarded guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article providing that ratification by conventions of nine States is sufficient to establish the Constitution among those States
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision 'The ratification of the conventions of nine States shall be sufficient for the establishment of this Constitution between the States, ratifying the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows the Constitution to take effect without unanimous ratification to avoid single-state veto of essential interests; grounds justification in necessity and principles of compacts/treaties and in differing ratification forms under the Confederation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: States shall not enter into treaties, alliances, or confederations
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall enter into any treaty, alliance, or confederation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copied from Articles of Confederation to preserve uniform foreign policy and prevent conflicting State treaties; part of a set of prohibitions protecting national coherence in foreign relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition/limitation: States shall not grant letters of marque and reprisal without federal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction on granting letters of marque; the new Constitution extends former prohibition so that such licenses must be obtained from the government of the United States both during war and before declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justified by need for uniformity in matters relating to foreign powers and for national responsibility for conduct; centralizes privateering authority to the federal level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: States shall not coin money
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall...coin money.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Left to States under Confederation as concurrent right; new provision removes State coinage to avoid multiplicity of mints and diverse forms/weights, which impede union and defeat uniform monetary policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: States shall not emit bills of credit (paper money)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall...emit bills of credit.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emitting paper money produced pestilent effects post-war (loss of confidence, injury to industry and morals); prohibition prevents such injurious State policies and associated animosities and injustices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: States shall not make anything but gold and silver a legal tender for debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall...make any thing but gold and silver a legal tender in payment of debts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounded on same reasons as prohibition on State paper currency; prevents retroactive changes to value and injury to other States' citizens and to subjects of foreign powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: States shall not pass bills of attainder, ex post facto laws, or laws impairing obligations of contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall...pass any bill of attainder, ex-post-facto law, or law impairing the obligation of contracts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are contrary to fundamental principles of social compact and sound legislation; prohibition acts as a constitutional bulwark for personal security and private rights and guards against legislative interference that becomes speculative or abusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: States shall not grant titles of nobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall...grant any title of nobility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copied from the Articles of Confederation; intended to prevent aristocratic distinctions incompatible with republican principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on State imposts/duties on imports/exports without Congress consent (with exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall, without the consent of the Congress, lay any imposts or duties on imports or exports, except what may be absolutely necessary for executing its inspection laws...' with the net produce to be for the use of the treasury of the United States and laws subject to Congressional revision and control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforces necessity of uniform trade regulation; prevents States from levying duties that would disrupt inter-state and foreign commerce; allows narrow exception for inspection laws but ensures revenue goes to federal treasury and that Congress can revise State laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction: States shall not, without Congress consent, lay duty on tonnage or keep troops/ships of war in time of peace
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall, without the consent of Congress, lay any duty on tonnage, keep troops or ships of war in time of peace...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents States from taking actions that would affect national maritime and defense policy; maintains federal control over military establishments and maritime charges in peacetime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction: States shall not enter into agreements/compacts with other States or foreign powers without Congress consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall...enter into any agreement or compact with another State, or with a foreign power...' without Congressional consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids conflicting inter-state or foreign agreements that could undermine national coherence; preserves federal oversight of inter-state compacts and foreign dealings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction: States shall not engage in war except when invaded or in imminent danger
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction 'No State shall...engage in war unless actually invaded, or in such imminent danger as will not admit of delay.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents unilateral State warfare; allows exceptional defensive action when invasion or imminent danger makes delay impossible.
